name: Northline Electric
headline: Power, planned around
the way you live.
lede: Thoughtful electrical work for remodels, additions, lighting, panels, EV charging and the systems behind modern Colorado homes.

proof.title: Plan before walls close
proof.desc: Coordinate load, lighting, controls and future capacity before rough-in becomes expensive to change.

proof.title: Document the decisions
proof.desc: Clear scopes, labeled systems and handoffs that make sense to homeowners, builders and the next trade in line.

proof.title: Finish like it belongs there
proof.desc: Devices, trims and lighting aligned to the architecture—not treated as an afterthought at the end of the job.

problems.label: The house is changing
problems.title: Renovation + addition planning
problems.desc: Rework circuits, loads, lighting and controls around the new plan before drywall locks in old assumptions.

problems.label: The lighting feels wrong
problems.title: Architectural lighting + controls
problems.desc: Layer task, ambient and accent light with controls that are intuitive at 6 a.m. and at midnight.

problems.label: The panel is out of room
problems.title: Service + panel strategy
problems.desc: Assess real demand, future loads and upgrade paths before buying hardware or opening walls.

problems.label: The garage needs to catch up
problems.title: EV charging + energy readiness
problems.desc: Plan charging around actual driving, panel capacity and the rest of the home’s future electrical load.

problems.label: The old wiring is a question mark
problems.title: Existing-system investigation
problems.desc: Trace, test and document what is actually there so the project can move forward with fewer surprises.

projects.title: A 1938 house, rewritten for modern loads.
projects.constraint: Original service, layered renovations and limited wall access.
projects.decision: Separate immediate safety work from future capacity; map new lighting and kitchen loads before finish selections.
projects.result: A phased electrical plan that let construction move without treating every discovery as an emergency.

projects.title: Quiet lighting for a house built around art.
projects.constraint: Large glass openings, reflective surfaces and a client who did not want visible ceiling clutter.
projects.decision: Use fewer fixture types, deliberate beam control and scene-based switching instead of more cans.
projects.result: Rooms that change character through the day without making the controls feel like a cockpit.

projects.title: Capacity for the car today—and the heat pump later.
projects.constraint: An EV charger request that would consume most of the existing service headroom.
projects.decision: Model future loads first, then sequence charging, panel and electrification work as one system.
projects.result: No duplicate upgrade work and a clear path for the next phase of the home.

process.title: Walk the problem
process.desc: Start on site with the plans, the existing conditions and the decisions that are still open.

process.title: Map the system
process.desc: Define loads, routes, controls, fixture intent and coordination points before work begins.

process.title: Build + document
process.desc: Execute cleanly, communicate changes early and keep the system understandable as the project moves.

process.title: Commission the home
process.desc: Test, label, tune scenes and walk the owner through the system before the project disappears into daily life.

faq.q: Can you join a project before construction starts?
faq.a: Yes. For remodels and additions, early coordination is usually where the most expensive rework can be avoided.

faq.q: Do you work with designers and builders?
faq.a: The demo strategy is built around coordinated residential work, with electrical decisions documented for the whole project team.

faq.q: Can you help decide what should be upgraded now versus later?
faq.a: Yes. The planning model separates urgent work, project-dependent work and future-capacity decisions so the scope can be sequenced intelligently.
